## M0 — Foundation

Workspace, CI gates, matrix gate, reference fetching and agent guard are in place and verified, so every later slice runs on trusted tooling.

| ID | Requirement | Kind | Source | Status | Depends on | Tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LIB-QA-001 | **CI runs every quality gate on three platforms.** Every push and pull request runs rustfmt, clippy (all targets, all features, -D warnings), the workspace and xtask tests on Linux, Windows and macOS, rustdoc with -D warnings, cargo-deny, the agent-hook tests and `cargo xtask matrix check`; any failure fails the build. | quality | Project policy (ADR 0002, ADR 0004) | `implemented` |  | `lib_qa_001_ci_runs_every_gate` |
| LIB-QA-002 | **MSRV 1.85 is declared consistently and checked.** The minimum supported Rust version is declared once in the workspace manifest, matches clippy.toml, and CI builds and tests the library and CLI with exactly that toolchain. | quality | ADR 0007 | `implemented` | LIB-QA-001 | `lib_qa_002_msrv_is_consistent` |
| LIB-QA-003 | **Dependency licences, advisories and sources are policed.** cargo-deny checks that every dependency has a licence compatible with distributing an MIT library, has no known security advisory, is not yanked, and comes from crates.io; CI runs it. | quality | Project policy (public MIT library) | `implemented` | LIB-QA-001 | `lib_qa_003_dependency_policy_is_enforced` |
| LIB-TOOL-001 | **Functionality-matrix gate.** `cargo xtask matrix check` enforces the rules of docs/matrix/README.md, `render` regenerates the Markdown view, and `next` lists the open rows whose dependencies are all verified, in milestone then file order. | tooling | ADR 0004 | `implemented` |  | `lib_tool_001_accepts_a_consistent_matrix`<br>`lib_tool_001_rejects_malformed_and_mismatched_ids`<br>`lib_tool_001_rejects_duplicate_ids`<br>`lib_tool_001_planned_rows_must_not_cite_tests`<br>`lib_tool_001_implemented_rows_need_acceptance_code_and_tests`<br>`lib_tool_001_test_citations_must_resolve_and_trace`<br>`lib_tool_001_verified_rows_need_record_and_verified_dependencies`<br>`lib_tool_001_rejects_cycles_and_backward_milestone_dependencies`<br>`lib_tool_001_unscheduled_rows_must_give_a_reason`<br>`lib_tool_001_reports_orphaned_traced_tests`<br>`lib_tool_001_detects_stale_rendered_page`<br>`lib_tool_001_next_lists_open_rows_with_verified_dependencies_in_order`<br>`lib_tool_001_finds_function_definitions_not_mentions`<br>`lib_tool_001_only_marked_tests_count_as_traced` |

## M1 — Minimal editable vertical slice

Create, load, validate, edit and save a strict SACM 2.3 document containing an AssuranceCasePackage, ArgumentPackage and Claims, with semantic round trip, structured diagnostics, safe XML handling and a CLI.

| ID | Requirement | Kind | Source | Status | Depends on | Tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LIB-API-002 | **Document, ElementId and typed navigation.** A `Document` owns one root interchange package and all elements under it; elements are identified by an `ElementId` newtype; users navigate by typed views (look up by id, iterate children by kind) without access to internal storage; `Document` and its views are `Send + Sync` and `Debug`. | api | docs/architecture.md (Model); D-ID | `planned` |  |  |
| LIB-API-003 | **Element kind metadata.** A public, non-exhaustive `ElementKind` enumerates every concrete SACM 2.3 class, reports its SACM class name and package, and answers is-a questions against the abstract superclasses (ModelElement, ArtifactElement, ArgumentAsset, Assertion, AssertedRelationship, ...). | api | ptc/22-03-13 (all packages); docs/sacm/metamodel-inventory.md | `planned` |  |  |
| LIB-API-004 | **Error types.** Operational failures (I/O, unreadable XML, rejected edits) are reported through documented, non-exhaustive error enums implementing `std::error::Error` with source chains; no public function panics on any input. | api | rust-library-craft skill (Errors vs diagnostics) | `planned` |  |  |
| LIB-DIAG-001 | **Structured diagnostics.** A `Diagnostic` carries a stable code, a severity (info, warning, error), the matrix row and clause it enforces, the affected element ids, an optional source location (line, column) and a message; diagnostics are returned in a deterministic order and implement `Display`. | api | D-DIAG; docs/sacm/diagnostics.md | `planned` |  |  |
